reference.source: Kaplan & Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry; DSM-5-TR
clinicalPearls: Characterised by excessive, hard-to-control worry about numerous everyday matters, present on most days over an extended period (on the order of six months or more)
Worry is accompanied by somatic and cognitive symptoms such as restlessness, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, and disturbed sleep
Patients frequently present first to primary care with physical complaints rather than naming anxiety as the problem
Distinguish from normal worry by the disproportionate intensity, pervasiveness, and functional impairment it causes
Exclude medical mimics such as hyperthyroidism, caffeine or stimulant excess, and arrhythmias, and screen for comorbid depression and substance use
First-line management combines cognitive behavioural therapy with pharmacotherapy, typically SSRIs or SNRIs as maintenance treatment
Benzodiazepines may give rapid short-term relief but carry dependence and tolerance risk and are avoided for long-term routine use
Comorbidity with depression and other anxiety disorders is common and worsens the overall burden
reference.pathophysiology: Generalized anxiety disorder involves dysregulation of fear and worry circuitry, particularly heightened amygdala reactivity with insufficient prefrontal regulation, alongside imbalances in gamma-aminobutyric acid, serotonin, and noradrenaline signalling. Genetic predisposition, temperamental traits such as behavioural inhibition, and chronic stress interact to produce a persistent state of anticipatory apprehension and autonomic arousal.
additionalDifferentials: Cardiac arrhythmia or other medical causes of palpitations
additionalInvestigations: Standardised anxiety rating scales to quantify severity and monitor response
Screening for depression and other anxiety disorders
Targeted cardiac evaluation when palpitations or chest symptoms predominate
redFlags: Emergent suicidal ideation, especially with comorbid depression
Escalating benzodiazepine or alcohol use to self-manage symptoms
New or severe physical symptoms suggesting an undiagnosed medical cause
Marked functional collapse or inability to work or care for self
reference.prognosis: Generalized anxiety disorder tends to be chronic and fluctuating, often worsening during periods of stress. Outcomes improve with sustained psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy, but comorbid depression and substance use are associated with greater chronicity and disability.
pitfalls: Relying on long-term benzodiazepines and creating dependence
Missing comorbid depression and its associated suicide risk
Ordering repeated investigations for somatic complaints without recognising the underlying anxiety disorder
Discontinuing effective antidepressant treatment prematurely and precipitating relapse
management: Cognitive behavioural therapy as the first-line psychological treatment, incorporating worry-focused techniques and applied relaxation
First-line pharmacotherapy with an SSRI or SNRI as maintenance treatment, allowing adequate time for response
Second-line pharmacological options such as pregabalin or buspirone, avoiding long-term benzodiazepine use because of dependence
Address modifiable contributors including caffeine and stimulant intake and exclude medical mimics such as hyperthyroidism
Identify and treat comorbid depression and substance misuse, which worsen chronicity and disability
Monitor severity and treatment response with standardised anxiety rating scales and assess suicide risk
Refer to specialist psychiatry or step up care for severe, refractory or highly comorbid presentations
